subject: Conditional fill color by pdf page

messages.author: 8f92b1b8d64c1a7d
messages.subject: Conditional fill color by pdf page
parts:
Hello,

I am plotting graphs page by page based on factor 'variable.' How can I make the fill color based on each value of variable?

For instance,

pdf('file.pdf')
for(i in variable){
plot <- ggplot(dplyr::filter(data, variable==i), aes(x, y) +
geom_bar(stat = 'identity', aes(fill = ??))
print(plot)
}
dev.off

Just entering fill = variable  does not work, it restarts the fill color for each page/graph.

Thanks!
Stefanie

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Conditional fill color by pdf page
parts:
Stefanie, 

You are supplying fill within the aes() call so if there is only one factor remaining in the dataset, it will be the same fill for every plot as you describe. 

In order to fill with different colors like you want to, you need to use the color scale functions to define those before your loop. Here is an example using the mtcars dataset:

library(tidyverse)

glimpse(mtcars) #look at example dataset
#similar example, want to split out different cyl
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(gear), fill = factor(cyl))) + geom_bar()



cyl = sort(unique(mtcars$cyl)) #define factor level for looping

colorcyl = scales::hue_pal()(length(cyl)) #gets Hex colours same length as factor levels of cyl

pdf('file.pdf') #open up pdf device
for(i in 1:length(cyl)){ #loop through cyl types
print( #have to print in a loop 
ggplot(dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl==cyl[i])) + #subset the data using loop
geom_bar(aes(x=factor(gear)), stat = 'count', fill=colorcyl[i])
)
} # end loop
dev.off() #close pdf device

Attached is the output. 

That said, for this dataset this is definitely not the "best" way to split this data. For example, if you have any hope of comparing cyl across gears (even if they are on different pages), you should fix the x and y axes across all of your plots. Faceting would allow you to do this even more easily, as would simply using colors and stacked or dodged bars. 

Depends on your goals and the connectedness of the data though. 

HTH, 
B

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Conditional fill color by pdf page
parts:
A simpler way is just to define the limits of a scale:

library(tidyverse)

cyls <- mtcars %>% split(.$cyl)
scale <- scale_fill_hue(limits = names(cyls))

for(cyl in cyls) {
p <- ggplot(cyl, aes(factor(gear), fill = as.character(cyl))) +
geom_bar() +
scale
print(p)
}

Hadley
